title: Why the band broke up: pay, road and buses
summary: Pay and the hard road led men to leave; the band held a meeting at the Harlem YMCA about leaking buses.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Did you leave it because of the pay policy?

Well, that was partly -- one of the reasons. I had misgivings about leaving it because I enjoyed playing with the guys in the band. At the same time when I was leaving it, other guys were leaving it too, Willie Smith and -- he had left it -- and Sy left first, going right for Tommy Dorsey.

And Sy made more just sitting down in New York writing for Tommy Dorsey then -- he made -- playing and writing, going all up and down the road with Lunceford, you know. He made a lot more. And one by one the guys started just leaving the band, and the money really did have a lot to do with it, the money proposition, but on top of that it was hard.

You know, we were out there all the time on the road. You had no kind of life because you were just moving year in, year out, all the time. And when you'd ask him about money -- in fact, we had a meeting once. I never forgot this -- in the YMCA-- on 135th Street in New York, up in Harlem once, about the terrible buses that we were riding in. The air leaked in. It rained in there sometimes.
So we had a meeting just to tell him we wanted decent transportation, and these are some of the things that took place then.
What happened after you told him?
He promised to do better, but it didn't -- nothing ever came of it.
